lines.text: You are unfinished.
Return to the Basin. Lie down. We will take the rest.
No.
Then it will hurt. Everything you carry will hurt.
Good. Then I'll know I'm still carrying it.
Hush. Don't stand so straight, they'll see the light in you.
You're the other one. The brother. I saw you run.
Where did they take him?
Down. The Low Gate, past the orchard, past the guards. He went talking.
The whole way. Telling the guards what he saw. He wanted them to hear it.
That's Tobiah.
The gate opens for the gathered and for the dropped. You're neither. You'll have to break it.
Keep count. The sun never sets here; it's the only way to know how long it's been.
I've been gathered twice. They put me back both times. "Not ripe." I don't ask what that means.
Stop there. I am... I am meant to stop you.
I sat down an hour ago. I can't remember why. Or how long an hour is.
You're a guard. Guard.
There's a song. I keep humming it. I don't know a single song. Angels don't.
Hum it.
(He hums. You know it.)
Where did you hear that?
From the one they dropped. He hummed it at the gate. I think... I think I knew it before that.
They say the Basin takes everything. It doesn't. Something stays in the hands.
Go on. I'll say I didn't see you. I'm good at not remembering.
This is the Low Gate. Nothing that goes through it comes back up.
He will.
The Garden will go on without you both. It always has.
A wooden harvest token, the kind the gathered carry to the Basin.
Someone has scratched a tally into the back: four strokes and a bar, over and over, until the wood ran out.
Torn from the Wardens' book. "Gathered this season: forty. Short of the Choir's need by three."
"Ungathered: one, dropped. Note the brother."
A curved piece of white stone, smooth as a bowl. It is warm.
When you hold it you cannot remember what you were thinking a moment ago.
Three thousand and twelve. Don't ask me what of. Suns, I suppose. Mine.
The orchard's full again. It fills up the day after a gathering. Nobody plants it.
(He hums. He stops when he notices you.) Still don't know it. Still can't stop.
My orders say 'none pass'. They don't say I have to stand up.
Sky. Under me, then over me. So that is what the floor of Purgatory is.
(A town under a torn sky. Fires. Something moving in the churchyard, and someone hammering.)
Someone is still here.
Don't stand in the light, lad. They see the light. ...You came down out of it, didn't you.
One hand. A brute took the other. I can still hammer; I can't hold the tongs. You hold, I hit. Deal?
What are we making?
Something that goes down and comes back. Nobody's managed the second part yet.
The sky opened a year ago. First the demons came up out of the churchyard. Then the angels came down. We thought that was help.
It wasn't help. They were gathering. Same as the demons, only cleaner about it.
I was one of them. Half of one.
I know. I've seen the hands. Yours haven't learned to hold yet.
That hook. Give it here.
Thigh bone and a hinge. That hinge is off the church door. I hung that door.
They're not animals, whatever Dace says. Animals don't use hinges.
Forty names on that paper. My wife's is the ninth. 'Called to the Garden early.'
When you get back up there, you tell me what garden.
Hold it steady. Steadier. Right, now don't move.
Good. That's one more they'll have to get through.
Keep your light down when you go in the ground. Both sides can see it.
I've a boy about your age. Had. Go on, I'm busy.
You're not from the sky. The sky ones don't jump, they just come down.
I'm Hanne. I draw what I see so I don't have to keep seeing it.
Want to see the big one's flag? Come back and I'll show you.
Here. It's not a picture. It's just lines.
(A tally mark. Four strokes and a fifth across.)
Where did you see this?
On the ones that climb. They cut it into themselves.
They say the Lowest says it means 'I'm still counting'.
That's the same lines. On your wooden coin. Did you cut them in yourself?
No. Someone counted me.
Then he's down there. The one who counts. Say hello from the drawing girl.
You went down. What's it like? I can't see down from here.
Pipes. White stone, going up through all of it. Like a kitchen's.
(She draws. Lines, going up.) Where do they go?
Here.
Did you find the one who counts?
His army. They're resting. They let me through.
Did you say hello from the drawing girl?
...Next time.
You said that like there's one.
Don't go near the churchyard. That's where they come up. I drew it. It's a bad one.
Pell says you're going down. Will you look at everything? I can't see down from here.
I counted the angels this morning. Nine. Yesterday it was eleven. Where do they go?
Halt. ...Halt doesn't work on your kind, does it. Fine.
Corporal Dace, Third Company. What's left of it.
Where's the rest?
In the ground. Some of them walking about in it.
Clock face. Church tower. Found it in a demon's pack. Don't know why it wanted it.
It's the only thing I've seen one of them carry that it didn't eat. Take it. Find out.
(A brass clock face with no hands. Four shapes are punched around the rim, where the hands would be pinned.)
You read Thorne's letter. He never sent it. I kept meaning to.
He's down there now. If you meet a lad in a red scarf, he was mine. Don't tell him I said so.
That's... (He holds it a long time before he takes it.)
You told him. I said don't. ...What did he say.
That the barricade held.
It did. It did hold.
You didn't tell him. Good. Good lad. He always did better not knowing who was watching.
He had a flask. Warden's glass, off one of the sky ones, full of their water. He said it closed cuts.
Take it. He'd want it going down, not sitting at a barricade with me.
They've stopped climbing. Three days now. Nothing out of the churchyard.
They're resting. All of them, in the eighth circle. Waiting on him.
Waiting for an order. I said. ...And when he gives it?
He won't.
Barricade's holding. Barricade's always holding, until it isn't.
They don't rush. They climb a bit, look at us, climb back. Like they're waiting for an order.
Clock's still ticking somewhere. I hear it at night. Nobody else does.
A church is where you go when you want to be heard. I stopped coming for that.
I stopped praying when I understood who was listening.
Who?
Someone who keeps a garden. And weeds it.
The demons shout upward when they climb. Not at us. Past us. A name. Every time the same name.
What name?
I won't say it in a church.
Outside, perhaps. If you come back up.
You've heard it now. It's on your face.
Then I'll say it, church or no. Tobiah. They shout it like a prayer. Perhaps it is one.
You've seen where the font drains. It's on your hands; you keep looking at them.
The Basin runs down into Hell.
Then it's one house. I had a feeling it was one house.
The warrant on the door is in the Choir's hand. I used to copy that hand. I taught it.
Pell swears, Dace counts, Hanne draws. I listen. Someone has to.
Go carefully. Below is only above with the lights put out.
Nailed to the church door. 'By the Choir's need, the following are called to the Garden early.'
Forty names. The ink is fresh.
Called early. Mereth was 'not ripe'. They're harvesting.
Demon-made, from a thigh bone and a hinge. The hinge is from a church door.
They came up with tools. Someone taught them.
Never sent. 'Mother, they say the ones in the ground were people once. I don't believe it. I don't want to.'
The churchyard. A hole, and warm air coming up out of it. Like a kitchen.
(From far below, faint: 'Up! He said up!')
Down, then.
You left your other half on the table in there.
Keep it.
We will. We keep everything.
Ungathered. You were seen at the Making. You will be finished.
You dropped my brother.
I have dropped many. I remember none of them. That is a mercy they give us.
The gate... does not open from this side.
I know. I'm not opening it.
(The Warden of the Low Gate lies still. Below the ledge, the gate waits for wings.)
A flat stone with eleven strokes scratched into it. The twelfth is half cut.
Somebody small was counting too.
'What is pressed is not lost. What is lost was never pressed. Sing it until it is true.'
Until it is true. They know it isn't.
Stiff with something that is not blood. The fingers are worn smooth on the inside, where they hold a head still.
They held mine. Halfway.
Names. Hundreds of them. Scratched going down.
(One, in a hand he knows: KEEP COUNT.)
I am.
You're going the wrong way. Everyone here is, but you're doing it on purpose.
What's at the bottom?
Whatever's left of you. The fall takes something at every circle. Fear first. Then names. Then faces.
By the bottom, teeth.
And if you hold on?
Then you'd be the first. I didn't try. I stopped here. Here's nothing, but it's mine.
The hand of a clock? Had it for ages. Someone fell past with it and let go.
Take it. Time's not a thing I need.
(A brass clock hand, bent at the tip. It is warm, like the shard.)
I wouldn't go to the Basin and I wouldn't fall. So they left me.
Turns out that's the one thing they can't do: make you choose.
Nothing comes back up this shaft. Nothing. I've watched a long time.
Someone your shape fell past, years back. Talking. Still talking when he was out of sight.
A finger bone with four cuts and a bar across them. The cuts are fresh.
They're counting. All of them.
Stop. Not to fight. He said a half-made thing would come down, and that I'm not to kill it.
Who said?
The Lowest. He doesn't say why. He says a lot of things and never why.
Go on. If you get past the seal, I'll have to try to kill you anyway. Orders only go so far.
Still here. Still not killing you. Don't make me find out how far orders go.
Below the seal is my ground. The Fury, they call me there. Up here I'm just waiting.
(Cut into the wall, deep, in a hand he knows: KEEP COUNT. DON'T FOLLOW. And a tally.)
Too late.
Memories. Buying. You've got a lot; I can smell them. Sell me the winter you died in. You won't miss it.
No.
That token, then. Someone below pays very well for anything with that mark. Doesn't say why. Pays, though.
Who?
Buyers don't give names. That one especially. Though he does say one. To himself. Not his.
Fresh ones, too. Come back when you want to be lighter. Everyone does, in the end.
The fall takes memories for free. I at least pay. Think about which of us is the thief.
Church iron. My own stock, and the last of it. Hold the blade on the horn. No, like that. Steadier.
There. It'll go through a brute's hide now, which is more than mine did.
What do I owe you?
More of it, if the ground has any. They hang their doors with it down there. Bring me a bar and I'll hammer it in.
That's church iron. Where did you... no. Don't tell me. Give it here.
Hold. Hit. Hold. Hit. ...That's as hard as I can make it, lad. The rest is you.
You asked me what garden. It's a farm. They have it in writing.
...A farm.
Then she was a crop. Say it. I'd rather hear it than guess it.
She was a crop.
Right. Hold the blade. Steadier. I've work to do.
The light over the churchyard went out a while this morning. First time in a year. That you?
The one who dropped my brother.
Good. One hand's enough to shake with.
You've been below the Seal. You've got a name now; I can smell it on you. Still want nothing?
A key. To a clock. You said you had one.
I did. For the winter you died in. Not the token; I've had a better offer for the token.
...Take it.
Done. You'll feel lighter. Everyone does. Here's your key; it was never mine to keep.
Lighter? Told you. There's a spring in there somewhere too, if you ever want to be rid of it.
Pipes. White stone pipes, going up. All the way up.
The Basin has to drain somewhere.
He came down past these. He saw them and kept going. Of course he did.
Go home, Ansel.
You first.
There isn't one. You've seen the pipes. You know what the Wheel is.
Then come and tell me. Not through this thing.
When you reach the floor. Not before. Keep count.
The floor, Ansel. Not before.
The angel's mouth moves. Nothing comes out of it now.
He's climbing with all of them, you know. All nine circles. To break the Basin.
He's not wrong. I'd just rather he did it without me.
Keep going. He's counting the days, and he thinks you are too.
A Choir tablet, in the same hand as the warrant. 'The Wheel is the Basin. Souls return to the Garden as the Choir's hands.'
'Teach the Wheel to the gathered; it calms them.'
Part of a clock that was never meant to run forward. Lead, and heavier than lead should be.
White stone, cut square, and cold. The inside is stained the colour of the Basin.
It drains to here. All of it.
Part of a clock that was never meant to run forward. Every link is stamped with a tally.
You're going the wrong way. ...I've said that before. To someone. I don't know who.
Is it holding? The barricade. I had a barricade, and a man who counted at it.
It's holding.
Good. Good. Then I'll stay here, and it'll hold.
You're going the wrong way. ...I've said that before. To someone. I don't know who.
A red scarf. You're Thorne. Third Company.
Thorne. (He says it twice, trying it on.) Was that the name? It fits in the mouth.
Is the barricade holding? I had a barricade, and a man who counted at it. He'd know.
Did he send you? Did he say anything?
He sent me. He said you were his. He said not to tell you.
(He laughs, and it is still a laugh.) That's him. That's the corporal.
Take the scarf. Red was the company. Tell him it held. Tell him I said the barricade held.
(Thorne's scarf. The red is the only colour in Violence that is not blood.)
Nobody sent me. I'm going down for my brother.
Then you'll pass my mother. Everyone's down here, in the end. (He unwinds the scarf.)
Take it anyway. Red was the company. If there's a man still counting at a barricade up there, he'll know whose.
(Thorne's scarf. The red is the only colour in Violence that is not blood.)
Is it holding?
Don't answer. I'd rather it held.
It's not cold here. People say it is. It's just that nothing's warm.
(The army, resting. Brutes step aside. Imps look up, and then down again. They know who he is.)
They are not going to stop you.
No. He told them not to.
Four hundred and something. Every one of them counted. He always finished a count.
(An imp holds out a tally bone like a gift.)
Keep it. Keep counting.
(The imp holds the bone up again, and waits.)
Nine circles' worth of names, in columns, each with a tally beside it. The last column is headed with four strokes and a bar.
Counted. Every one of them.
A harvest token, the twin of the one from the Garden. Four hundred and ten strokes, and room for none.
You kept count.
Every day.
How many?
I don't know. There was a page. The token ran out of wood.
Four hundred and nine. I kept it too.
Come home.
Ansel. Say what home is. Say it out loud.
It's a farm. You've seen the ledger. You've seen the pipes. We were on a list.
Then we'll go somewhere else.
There is nowhere else. There's up and there's down. I'm going up, with everyone they threw away, and I'm going to break the Basin.
They'll make you into one of them. Or they'll drop you again.
Then stop me. You've got the light for it. They gave you half of it.
I don't want to.
I know. That's why it has to be you.
Well. You've still got the better arm.
Get up.
Can't. That's all right. I counted. Four hundred and ten. One more than I thought I'd get.
(Ansel carries Tobiah up through nine circles. The demons let them pass.)
(Tobiah talks the whole way, then stops talking somewhere around the Shallows. Ansel keeps climbing.)
(The Low Gate, from below.)
Then I'll keep counting.
Start at one.
(The army climbs without them. The sound of the climb fades.)
(The five pieces fit. The face, the hand, the weight, the chain, the key.)
That is not a clock.
No. It's the only thing in all of this that runs backward.
If you turn it, you will not have been made. You will not have the light. You will not be able to come down here.
Then I won't need to.
(Ansel on the orchard edge. The sound of two boys arguing, far off. One of them is him.)
Don't look. Don't go to him. He hasn't heard anything yet.
Keep count.
(A clock, or the frame of one, with pieces missing. It does not run either way.)
Five. Keep count.
Child. You are not from this day.
No.
I made you. Or I will. The light in you is mine; I know my own.
Why the Basin?
I was the first. There was no one to wipe me. So I remember being hungry, and I remember the Making, and I remember nothing else.
A heaven must be for something. I could not think what. So it is for me.
It was for us.
Then take it.
(The light goes out of the first angel like a lamp. The Making stops. The harvest stops.)
(The sun sets in the Garden for the first time. Dark. Stars.)
Ansel. Ansel, look. What is that?
Night.
What's it for?
Counting, I think. Start at one.
(The bottom of the churchyard. The hole goes down past where the lantern light stops, and the hammering is far above now.)
This is the way down. Nothing that goes this way comes back up the same.
Then I'll come back different. Keep count.
I told you. Orders only go so far.
He asked me. Every day. 'Has a half-angel come down.' Every day, like I'd forget.
He said you'd come. He said your name. He says it when he thinks nobody's there.
Say his.
The Lowest doesn't have one.
Say it.
...Tobiah.
Then I'll bring him home.
Home. You still think that's a place.
I chose the fall. I chose it. Let me finish choosing.
Down, then. At last. Thank you.
Don't thank me.
